extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary critics, and serious readers of late-19th-century poetry and fiction
extracted.subtask_description: Critical assessment of poetry and fiction—standards and aesthetic criteria used by a literary reviewer (Walter Pater) to judge poets and novelists, focusing on originality, technique, descriptive power, historical verisimilitude, tone, and characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of motive and subject
rubrics_metrics.description: The accomplished group of poets to which he belongs requires, above all, novelty of motive, of subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pater praises poets who bring new motives or subjects even when working with old themes. He contrasts novelty with mere learned grace: originality may be subtle or unconscious rather than theatrical. (Example: Mr. Gosse's use of northern and Thames-side subjects as fresh motives.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Purely descriptive power (still-life and landscape)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purely descriptive power, aptitude for still-life and landscape, is unmistakably vivid and sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the writer's ability to render place and scene concretely and vividly. Pater cites Mr. Gosse's high-northern summer stanza as an instance (ice-white mountains, creeping sallows, cranberry-flowers). Authentic acquaintance with subject-matter (e.g., northern lands) strengthens descriptive authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical command of poetic craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete command of the technique of poetry—every form of what may be called skill of hand in it: delicate cadences, delicate transitions of thought, faculty of structure, the logic of poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess fluency in forms, metre, cadence, transitions, and overall structural logic. Pater points to 'The New Endymion' as an example of sustained technical power. Technical mastery should enable balance and sustained effects rather than mere mannerism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of matter and form; variety of effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The perfect balance his work presents of so many and varied effects, as regards both matter and form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for equilibrium between thematic substance and formal technique; a variety of effects harmonised into a coherent whole. Excessive emphasis on either matter or form undermines the work's grace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic scholarship and blended allusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Memories of a large range of poetic reading are blent into one methodical music so perfectly that at times the notes seem almost simple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive: wide reading and learned allusion can be integrated so they enrich the work's music and texture. Negative: such scholarship may bring inherited 'faults' (e.g., 'spasmodic' lapses) if it becomes imitative or mechanical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spontaneous (unconscious) originality
rubrics_metrics.description: The sense of his originality comes to one as but an after-thought; he has made no conscious effort to be original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality is valued when it appears natural and unforced. Consciously hunted novelty is less admirable than originality that arises from temperament and sincere vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transforming classical forms into modern/local contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: He transforms, by a kind of colour-change, classic forms and associations into those—say! of Thames-side—pieces which, though in manner or subject promising a classic entertainment, almost unaware bring you home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise works that adapt classical models to contemporary or local subjects so that classical manner enriches present-day feeling without mere pastiche. This transformation should feel seamless and illuminating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate tone for life stages and moods
rubrics_metrics.description: Although he sings much of youth, he is often most successful in the forecast, the expression, of the humours, the considerations, that in truth are more proper to old age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether tone and perspective suit the ages or moods depicted (e.g., sympathetic, measured expression of old-age sensibilities). Tone must be convincing for the life stage it represents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophic/aesthetic coherence (worldview in the work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes of Epicurean philosophy fall almost unconsciously from his lips; a large faith in 'natural optimism'—the beauty and benignity of nature, if let alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a consistent philosophical or aesthetic stance (e.g., natural optimism, Epicureanism) is embedded in the poetry and whether it coheres with the poet's images and tone. Consider implications (e.g., the poet's treatment of individuality and oblivion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained power in long compositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty of structure, the logic of poetry. 'The New Endymion' is a good instance of such sustained power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge a poet's ability to maintain structural and tonal coherence over longer forms; sustained imaginative and technical control is a mark of high poetic scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dignified, authentic characterization (clerical and peasant types)
rubrics_metrics.description: He has delineated, with wonderful power and patience, a strictly ecclesiastical portraiture—shrewd, passionate, somewhat melancholy heads... the secular brothers and sisters ... are shown with great acquaintance with the sources, the effects, of average human feeling; priests are never by any chance undignified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess character-drawing for truthfulness, dignity, and restraint—especially when portraying social or religious types. Avoid caricature; strength lies in faithful, humane depiction even when critiquing institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid regional setting and atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: For his background he has chosen, has made his own and conveys very vividly to his readers, a district of France... The large towns, the sparse hamlets, the wide landscape of the Cevennes... are what his books have.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the author's capacity to render a locale's distinct atmosphere—landscape, customs, light, color—so that setting becomes integral to character and theme (example: Fabre's Cevennes; Gosse's Arctic summer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of antiquarian/historical detail with tact and economy
rubrics_metrics.description: With a sympathetic sense of life as it is, M. Filon has transplanted the creations of his fancy into an age... where a fully detailed antiquarian knowledge, used with admirable tact and economy, is indeed serviceable in giving reality of effect to scene and character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical and antiquarian details should serve verisimilitude and imaginative life without overwhelming narrative. Pater praises Filon's intimate antiquarianism when it secures imaginative cooperation of the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lightness of touch and economy of manner
rubrics_metrics.description: With perfect lightness of touch, M. Filon seems to have a complete command of all the physiognomic details of old France... With perfect lightness of touch, M. Filon seems to have a complete command...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value subtlety, restraint, and economy in presentation: small, well-chosen details and a graceful handling that avoids heavy-handed description. Lightness aids charm and readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minute presentment of life; picturesque, human detail
rubrics_metrics.description: A series of delightfully picturesque studies which aim at the minute presentment of life in France under the old regime... his very lively antiquarianism carries with it a genuine air of personal memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise careful, small-scale observational scenes that illuminate permanent human concerns. Minute detail should enrich character and theme rather than function as mere antiquarian showmanship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing antiquarian knowledge with direct human interest
rubrics_metrics.description: A delicacy which keeps his large yet minute antiquarian knowledge of that vanished time ever in service to a direct interest in humanity as it is permanently, alike before and after '93.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticize works where historical curiosity overwhelms the human story. The ideal is that learned detail supports emotional and moral engagement with characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of narrative device to mediate history (voice and form)
rubrics_metrics.description: It was a happy thought of M. Filon to put into the mouth of an imaginary centenarian a series of picturesque studies... a genial centenarian ... appreciates both vanished surface detail and permanent humanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate appropriateness and effectiveness of narrative framings (e.g., letters, a centenarian narrator) for delivering historical material and shaping reader sympathy and perspective. Effective devices harmonize distance and intimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of everyday rituals as meaningful
rubrics_metrics.description: With the peasant of the Cevennes the meal is what nature meant it to be—a few moments for self-recovery after fatigue, a short space of silence of a quite elevated character, almost sacred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether quotidian acts and rituals are depicted with reverence and depth, making ordinary behavior reveal character, culture, and moral tone instead of trivializing it.
